input.mechanism: Order flow imbalance amplification during low liquidity periods predicts short-term price continuation.
input.falsifiable_prediction: If order flow imbalance is in the top decile and bid-ask spread is above its median, then price moves further in the same direction over the next 15-60 minutes more often than random.
input.market_structure_assumption: Markets exhibit periods of liquidity shortage where aggressive order flow has amplified price impact, consistent with inventory risk models.
input.instrument_scope: FTMO MT5 forex majors (EURUSD, GBPUSD, USDJPY) and equity indices (US30, US100, US500).
input.required_data: Tick or M1 data with bid/ask and volume/tick direction to compute order flow imbalance and spread.
input.expected_trade_frequency: Unknown; depends on extreme imbalance frequency.
expected_failure_modes: Order flow imbalance may not be computable from standard MT5 tick data without direction classification.
Liquidity proxy (spread) may be noisy or not correlate with true liquidity.
Effect may be too small after estimated transaction costs.
May not generalize from Treasury to forex/equity index markets.
invalidation_criteria: No statistically significant price continuation following extreme OFI+spread conditions in out-of-sample walk-forward analysis.
Net return after estimated spread and swap costs is not positive over out-of-sample period.
Signal performance indistinguishable from random entry in bootstrap test.
input.implementation_shape: Compute rolling OFI as sum of tick direction * volume over 30-min lookback; compute spread as (ask-bid)/mid; enter long when OFI > 90th percentile and spread > median; exit after 30 minutes or when OFI turns negative.
input.execution_sensitivity: Sensitive to tick data quality, spread widening during news, and swap costs on held positions.
input.mt5_ftmo_concerns: FTMO may not provide tick-level bid/ask history for all instruments; spread calculation may be imprecise; swap charges may erode profits on longer holds.
